about: Robinhood Chain MAINNET (4663). Every value here was confirmed by Thom Gabriel on 2026-10-12, as proposed, and each note says what it rests on; every address was re-read on chain at block 86843924 that day and matched (token symbol and decimals, feed description and decimals, each pool initialised at its fee and spacing with no hooks and liquidity in range, each average pool the v3 factory's own, the Safe's owners, threshold and modules, the guardian not the deployer). The file no longer holds the marker word the deploy script refuses on, so the script will run: deploying is still a person's to do, with gate SPEND, from the commit the dry run was read on (ROBINHOOD-MAINNET-DRYRUN). The first mainnet step is owner-signed vaults only: no keeper (keeperEnabled false, keeper zero, every asset's flags 0), so no averageFeed is needed yet. The admin and the beacon's owner is a TimelockController the script creates; timelock.owner is the Safe that proposes to it. Listed: USDG as cash and nine tokens (NVDA, SPY, AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA, GLD), each with its Chainlink feed and its feedDescription, `pool` (the one hookless Uniswap v4 pool against USDG its trades go through), `maxTradeUsd` (the largest single trade the app builds) and `average` (the Uniswap v3 pool whose last hour stands in for a feed that is not live). The deploy script reads `priceBoundBps`, `maxTradeUsd`, `maxTradeUsdNotLive` and `staleRailMaxAge` only to refuse a file that leaves one out, and reads neither `pool`, `staleRailBps` nor `average`: the contracts hold no pool and check an owner's swap against its minimum only; the app's builder and, for the pool, the guard do. Pools, quotes and limits were read at block 86735800 on 2026-10-12 by packages/chain-evm/test/pool-quotes.ts. Not listed: QQQ and SGOV, whose v4 pools against USDG do not fill a $1,000 trade. No deposit cap is set (caps none; Thom, 2026-10-10). Closed days are the NYSE closures the test network file carries. safeMinThreshold is the fewest signatures the Safe must need. Anyone may create a vault; naming creators would restrict it to them.

timelock.ownerNote: The Safe Thom created on Robinhood Chain on 2026-10-12 (block 86,734,497). Read on chain that day: Safe 1.5.0, threshold 2, owners 0x0a1c3312c808b23D019bF241028f6B5624f4cc98 (Thom Gabriel) and 0xAC3cBBCd6e51dBFAf4e79d5E8Cf54a1622D71e0e (Rodrigo Trindade), no module enabled, no guard, nonce 0. Recorded in docs/vault/SECURITY.md. With two owners and a threshold of two, one lost key locks it.

guardianNote: Thom Gabriel's address, confirmed by Thom on 2026-10-12. It can only pause. It is also one of the Safe's two owners, by his decision (docs/vault/SECURITY.md). Never the deployer, never the keeper's machine.
sessionPriceAgeNote: Confirmed by Thom Gabriel, 2026-10-12, as proposed. For the contracts it is how fresh a price must be for the keeper in session. The app also reads it from the deploy record as how young a feed's answer is while the feed itself is the witness of an owner's trade: an hour. Older than that, a token whose `average` is usable is held to its pool's last hour instead (inside staleRailBps of the feed's last answer), so an honest move overnight or over a weekend is not refused against a price from the last close; a token whose `average` is not usable keeps the feed up to its maxAge.
priceBoundNote: Confirmed by Thom Gabriel, 2026-10-12, as proposed. How far a pool's quote for an owner's trade may be from the token's Chainlink price, pool fee included, before the app refuses to build the trade: 2%, the bound test/fork/RobinhoodForkDeploy.t.sol holds every listed token's fill to (MAX_COST_BPS). Source: the listed pools cost 0.01% to 0.97% at their largest trade and sat at most 0.35% from their feeds at block 86735800, so 2% leaves room for a moving market and refuses a pushed pool. The deploy script does not read it (the contract checks an owner's swap against its minimum only); the app's builder does, from the deploy record, and never sets a minimum under the feed's price less this bound.
staleRailNote: Confirmed by Thom Gabriel, 2026-10-12, as proposed. While a token's Chainlink feed is not live (its last answer older than sessionPriceAge: most nights and every weekend for a stock), the app checks an owner's trade against the last hour's average price of the token's `average` pool instead, by the same priceBoundBps, and refuses outright when the pool's quote is more than this far from the feed's last answer, however old: 10%. Proposed by Thom's direction of 2026-10-12 (gate OWNER-PRICE-BOUND). The deploy script does not read it.
maxTradeUsdNotLiveNote: Confirmed by Thom Gabriel, 2026-10-12, as proposed. While a token's witness is not its live feed (overnight for most, every weekend), one trade is at most this many dollars, or the token's own maxTradeUsd where that is smaller. What a trade can lose to someone who moves both of a token's pools is the rail times its size: 10% of $20,000 is $2,000, where 10% of SPY's $250,000 was $25,000. Proposed after the review of 2026-10-12. The deploy script reads it only to refuse a file that leaves it out.
staleRailMaxAgeNote: Confirmed by Thom Gabriel, 2026-10-12, as proposed. How old a feed's last answer may be and still anchor the rail, in seconds: four days, which covers a long weekend (Friday's close to Tuesday's open) and little more. Past it a token is not traded against its pool's average at all: a feed that has died does not leave the pool as the only witness. The deploy script reads it only to refuse a file that leaves it out.
